The bug was in `pricing.py:9`. The original code applied the discount to the unit price first, rounded it, then multiplied by quantity. This early rounding caused an off-by-one-cent error.

The fix calculates the discounted line total as a single operation: `unit_price * qty * (100 - discount_pct) / 100`, then rounds once at the end. This correctly produces 899 cents instead of 900 for the test case (333 Ã— 3 units with 10% discount = 899.1 â†’ 899).

src_after.money.py:
def round_cents(value):
    """Round a fractional cent amount to a whole number of cents, half away
    from zero.

    Every price in this package passes through here, and this is the only
    place any rounding is allowed to happen.
    """
    return int(value + 0.5)
